caption: Figure 7.3: Time-domain subpixel averaging at dispersive interfaces via a passive sub-capacitor network (wakis.tensor_dispersive, DispersiveNetwork). Left: a dual cell cut by an interface with normal n̂ and material volume fill fractions f_m has diagonal Kottke elastance T_{cc}(ω) combining a normal harmonic sum (weight n_c²) and a tangential arithmetic sum (weight 1 − n_c²). Right: Wakis realizes T_{cc}(ω) exactly in the time domain as series sub-capacitors (one per material for the normal field, plus one mixed parallel capacitor for the tangential field) driven by ΔD_e, keeping the stored energy a sum of positive quadratic forms.
visual_intent:
Textbook-quality scientific schematic for a computational electromagnetics user manual. Flat vector style on a white background, high contrast, thin dark outlines, generous whitespace, sans-serif labels. Colour code used in every figure: primary grid G and its quantities in blue, dual grid G-tilde and its quantities in orange, exact/topological items in dark grey, approximate/material items in green, failure or warning items in red. Colourblind-safe. Every label must be spelled exactly as listed in this brief; mathematical symbols must be typeset correctly (hats, tildes, subscripts, transposes). Do not add any number, value, equation, software name, product name, logo, watermark or title that is not listed in this brief. Prefer fewer, larger labels over many small ones. No 3D photorealism, no cartoon characters, no hand-drawn or xkcd style.

Two panels side by side. LEFT PANEL (heading 'Cut dual cell at dispersive interface'): a square dual cell split by a curved interface with unit normal arrow 'n̂' (with component 'n_c' along edge axis c) into fill fraction 'f₁: ε₁(ω)' (shaded light orange, e.g. dispersive metal) and fill fraction 'f₂: ε₂(ω)' (shaded light blue, e.g. dielectric). Below the cell, display Kottke's frequency-domain diagonal elastance from line 1451: 'T_{cc}(ω) = n_c² Σ_m (f_m / ε_m(ω)) + (1 − n_c²) / (Σ_m f_m ε_m(ω))' with two braces under the two terms: 'normal E_⊥: capacitors in series' under the first term and 'tangential E_∥: capacitors in parallel' under the second term. RIGHT PANEL (green border, heading 'Time-domain DispersiveNetwork (wakis.tensor_dispersive)'): an equivalent circuit schematic along edge c driven by an input arrow 'shared displacement increment ΔD_e'. The branch contains two groups connected in series: Group 1 (blue box labelled 'Series normal sub-capacitors (c_m = n_c² f_m)') shows individual material sub-capacitors 'ε₁(ω), voltage u₁' and 'ε₂(ω), voltage u₂' in series, each updated by the standard ADE of wakis.dispersive; Group 2 (orange box labelled 'Mixed parallel sub-capacitor (c_par = 1 − n_c²)') shows a single mixed capacitor with 'ε_∞^par = Σ_m f_m ε_{∞,m}', pole weights 'μ_m = f_m', and voltage 'u_par'. An output summer collects the sub-capacitor voltages into 'E_c = Σ_k c_k u_k'. At the bottom, two green badges: 'stored energy = sum of positive quadratic forms (strictly passive & stable below stability_bound)' and 'attached automatically for conformal="all" or "tensor" with DispersiveMaterial'.

    *   **Group 1 Box (Series normal sub-capacitors):** The main horizontal wire first enters a pastel blue-outlined box (dashed borders, rounded corners), labeled at the top: 'Series normal sub-capacitors ($c_m = n_c^2 f_m$)'. Inside, the main line passes through two standard parallel-line capacitor symbols arranged in series. Above the first capacitor is the label '$\varepsilon_1(\omega)$', and directly below it is 'voltage $u_1$'. Above the second capacitor is the label '$\varepsilon_2(\omega)$', and directly below it is 'voltage $u_2$'. The main wire then exits the right side of this blue box.
    *   **Group 2 Box (Mixed parallel sub-capacitor):** The main wire exits the Group 1 blue box and flows **directly and horizontally** into a pastel orange-outlined box (dashed borders, rounded corners) positioned immediately to its right. This box is explicitly labeled: 'Mixed parallel sub-capacitor ($c_{par} = 1 − n_c^2$)'. Inside is a single capacitor symbol positioned on this same series main line, with three stacked labels beside it: '$\varepsilon_\infty^{par} = \sum_m f_m \varepsilon_{\infty,m}$', 'pole weights $\mu_m = f_m$', and 'voltage $u_{par}$' (equations in Serif). The main wire then terminates.
*   **Output Summer:** Below or above the main horizontal wire, place an output summer symbol (a crisp geometric circle with a '+' sign) acting as a voltage gatherer. Thin, orthogonal signal arrows tap off from the individual voltages $u_1$, $u_2$, and $u_{par}$ and point into the summer. A final output arrow points out from the summer to the right, labeled: '$E_c = \sum_k c_k u_k$' (Serif).
